articleTitle: Cloud based Real-Time Data Acquisition for Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: We propose a solution for Real-Time data management from sensors to Cloud. For this approach we connect sensors to a NI CompactRIO<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> and using a NI LabVIEW<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> program, we will be able to extract all data collected from the sensors and save it to a Cloud location, using NI SystemLink Cloud. We can store all recorded data (waveforms and labels) into files, for example TDMS files, applying all required analytics, for example: data visualizations, data analytics, artificial intelligent algorithms. Also, the TDMS files can be opened for visualization with NI DIAdem. This configuration was used for a real case, but this approach is generic enough to be applied for all cases when transfer data directly to Cloud is needed.

articleTitle: Electronic Hive Management System for a Beekeeping Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper aims to digitize the beekeeping field, allowing the monitoring of hives and facilitates beekeeper intervention in a vehicle used to transport bees’ families between flowering areas. The system is based on the “master – slave” principle, using the main/master unit to process and display the information received from the secondary/slave units on a designated touchscreen. In order to achieve system accessibility, three levels of slave units (low-mid-high) and a microcontroller programmer used by the slave units were developed. The scientific and technical work consists in the development of the system, from schematic conception to printed circuits design and manufacturing, assembling, and testing of the whole system for proper operation in a real-life environment.

articleTitle: System for Electronic Control Unit Sniffing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In this study is proposed an electronic module that connects to a vehicle's CAN Bus communication bus via the vehicle's OBD II diagnostic port. It scans the ECU (Electronic control unit) and retrieves On-board diagnostics Parameter IDs “PID” supported by the vehicle. These parameters are then stored via the SD card module in a memory card so that they can be used for vehicle diagnostics and testing of the functions supported by the ECU. The information that is being retrieved includes the speed of the communication bus, the ID or name of the ECU number of captured PIDs, their identical numbers, their class, the parameters they represent and their values.

articleTitle: Acoustic Vibration Measurement System based on a Microphone Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In addition to the essential role that sound signals play in the interaction between the human beings, they are the basis of many other applications in our daily lives such as communications, medical applications, monitoring and security systems, voice assistants or entertainment [1]. Therefore, their acquisition and processing have been a field of high interest in recent years. Considering this aspect, the goal of this paper is to propose a system that allows both the acquisition and analysis of sound signals, through an easy-to-use graphical interface, as well as their programmable amplification, depending on the applications of interest. The proposed system is based on an array consisting of 12 high-performance analog micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS) microphones and the ShieldBuddy TC275 development board, which offers advantages both in terms of the sensitivity of the system and the capacity to acquire and process the captured sound signals.

articleTitle: A VR Environment to Build Simulators for Records in Control Plan
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The objective of the paper is to present a framework built on VR (Virtual Reality) technology used to simulate the test processes that operators must implement according to the control plan. The control plan represents a stage that follows the FMEA analysis and in which the test measures are presented to reduce the risk of failures. Until this moment, the developed control plan listed the test and measurement methods that were then displayed to the operators for implementation. What we propose is that each recording in the control plan be associated with a VR simulation through which the operator can train on how to apply measures/methods to reduce faults in the manufacturing process and a 3D film through which the client can observe the measurement process in a form as close as possible to reality. These things are possible by using the framework created and presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Design of a Laboratory Platform for Buck-Boost Converter Characterization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: An important part of practical engineering is understanding converters. To help students, theoretical presentations should be supported by simulations and measurements on real modules. As part of a lab on DC-DC converters, a platform was developed to allow students to observe the operation of a buck-boost converter. Students should first read and understand the basic operation of the circuit, use formulas to determine the expected values for the output voltage in different modes, simulate the converter in Spice, and then use the board to compare the previously obtained values with the real values they can observe with an oscilloscope or measure with a multimeter.

articleTitle: Real-time Data Analysis Using Industrial Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents a detailed analysis of the network for temperature and vibration sensors installed for monitoring automotive transmission test equipment. Recent results show that wireless vibration sensors are a better alternative than wired sensors. After a year of analysis and research, we can assess the strengths and weaknesses as well as the capabilities of such a network. The result is excellent: no more unexpected downtime of our assembly lines and this with minimal effort and budget. The proposed network can be extended to almost all machines and workstations, it can detect possible damages, imbalances or misalignments. This allows easier and more convenient planning of long-term maintenance, manpower or spare parts needs.

articleTitle: The Influence of Temperature on the Efficiency of a Mini Photovoltaic Panel
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This study focuses on the analysis of efficient operation of photovoltaic panels, in conditions of artificial variations of the ambient temperature. For this, a small chamber equipped with a heating system and a temperature monitoring system was used. The panels were positioned inside the chamber, provided with insulating glass walls, allowing light to penetrate, making possible the generation of solar energy. The system is also provided with a light intensity monitoring sensor to be sure that the light does not decrease in intensity. The temperature was modified between 34 and 70 degrees Celsius. NI USB 6008 and LabVIEW were used to acquire the signals, the temperature sensor (thermocouple K) and light intensity sensor (phototransistor) for monitoring the respective parameters. Based on the proposed temperature variation, it was found that the voltage value at the cell terminals decreases significantly with the increase in temperature.

articleTitle: Comparison between the Electrical Parameters of High Voltage Supercapacitor Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Nowadays, the supercapacitor plays a crucial role in the storage and generation of electrical energy. It also serves as an effective solution for renewable energy storage. Against the backdrop of the energy crisis, more emphasis is being placed on developing and improving components that maximize charge storage, ensure long life, and deliver energy on demand. Based on its capabilities, the supercapacitor appears to meet all of these requirements and be a viable alternative to other electrical charge storage devices on the market. Recent research in this area has focused on improving the parameters of supercapacitors, especially by increasing the maximum working voltage of a single cell. In this paper, we present a comparative study of the parameters of supercapacitor cells with increased voltage (above 2.5 V) made with different types of electrolytes and activated carbon-based electrodes. For this study, 6 supercapacitor cells with 3 types of electrolytes (2 cells each) were fabricated and tested.

articleTitle: Implementing Power Resistors on Aluminium Core Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Power resistors are key components in industrial applications that operate at high currents. Standard components of this type are available from various manufacturers, but they can also be easily implemented as traces on a printed circuit board, especially when the required resistance is in the range of 1…10 ohms. By using aluminum core technology for PCBs, heat transfer is better and allows higher power ratings. Our paper presents the design, implementation and testing of such resistors fabricated on Al-core PCBs using traces with the shape of a Hilbert curve. Electrical and thermal measurements are performed for various configurations of PCB trace resistors.

articleTitle: Comparative Studies of Temperature Influence on Characteristics of Dye Sensitized and Silicon Based Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper continues our investigations on dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs), or Grätzel cells, presented in references [1] and [2]. We will present the influence of temperature on the current-voltage characteristics of DSCC produced after a proprietary process, and for comparison, we will measure in identical conditions some selected commercial silicon-based photovoltaic cells. Derived parameters such as short-circuit current, open-circuit voltage, fill factor, maximum power point, series resistance, and parallel resistance will also be presented. The results of the research will contribute to the development of the DSCC production process, with a focus on the materials. In this study, we have tested four different solar cells at various temperature conditions: an amorphous silicon solar cell designed for indoor applications produced by Panasonic, a silicon based solar cell, a dye-sensitized solar cell with a structure based on titanium dioxide that was produced by our colleagues from the National Institute of Research and Development for Electrochemistry and Condensed Matter, in Timisoara, by following the procedures in [2] and [3], and a flexible solar cell for indoor applications produced by PowerFilm Solar.

articleTitle: Embedded system for charging alkaline batteries
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: A well-known and debated topic recently is related by batteries and chargers. Batteries are used in a wide variety of fields like automotive electric vehicles where new technologies are continuously researched but also house hold items where we can find different types like li-ion and alkaline batteries. For most of the rechargeable batteries there are different types of chargers each having different features like fast charge or smart charger and so on. Like any other consumable, the battery also reaches the end of its life after a number of charging cycles or other wear factors. After the batteries degrade and can no longer be used it needs to be recycled. The recycling process is still a researched process because it also causes pollution and it is not completely green. Some of the batteries like alkaline small ones can only be used once and the manufacturer states that no one should attempt to charge a non-rechargeable battery. Well, most of them can be recharge by using a system based on a microcontroller and software that knows how to manage the current and voltage of the charging process. By managing to recharge depleted batteries can also contribute to fewer waste and a greener planet. In our researched we are proposing an algorithm and a system for recharging small alkaline batteries which can be reused for many cycles.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Analysis of a Network of Sensors and Energy Consumption Optimization Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The correct functioning of the circuits depends on the energy consumption, but nevertheless it is essential that this consumption be reduced as much as possible, but not to values that can affect the functionality and performance of these electronic circuits. Currently, methods of saving energy consumption is an active field of research and there are different methods by which power can be reduced in circuits, even from the design level. In this work, the energy consumption of a development board set in different operating modes is analyzed with the help of the KWS-v20 tester. Even if energy saving methods exist, we must also analyze whether they are sufficient by determining consumption values. Sensors for monitoring the various parameters that are to be analyzed in a sensor network are energy consumers and therefore saving energy consumption is very important for the correct and long-term operation of this sensor network.

articleTitle: Mechanical Response of Type 2 Multi-Layer Ceramic Capacitors Under Different Electric Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper aims to provide insight into the mechanical behaviour of Type 2 MLCCs (Multi-Layer Ceramic Capacitors) under different electrical loads. Considering that these capacitors utilize BaTiO3 as a dielectric material, which possesses well-known piezoelectric properties, applying an electrical signal to the terminations of the MLCCs shall generate a mechanical response. To examine this phenomenon, the MLCCs are positioned at various locations on a test PCB (Printed Circuit Board), and a correlation between the electrical signal and the mechanical response (e.g., displacement) is established. As this is one of the main causes of the capacitor’s singing phenomenon, the study aims to provide resourceful data for further analysis of the behaviour of Type 2 MLCCs. An in-depth analysis of the piezoelectric phenomenon present in MLCCs is also described.

articleTitle: Thermocouple Fabrics for Energy Harvesting in Smart Textiles –Applications and Prototype
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Aim of this paper is to outline some recent developments in the field of textile integrated thermoelectric generators (TEGs), with focus on the final applications and to present two small prototypes developed at INCDTP – Bucharest. TEGs represent an autonomous energy harvesting solution to be integrated within a textile material with the purpose of supplying small devices of smart textiles (sensors, actuators, antennas etc.). Pairs of metallic threads were sewn onto a textile substrate in order to construct a thermopile: Silver and Copper/Silver threads for the first prototype and Silver and Stainless steel threads for the second prototype. The two parts of the textile substrate were subjected to a temperature gradient (up to 80K) and the generation of a voltage was evidenced in the range of $50- 160 \mu \mathrm{V}$. This is a promising result for continuation of experiments with different types of threads and different geometrical structures.

articleTitle: The Reuse of Food Loss and Waste in the Viticulture Sector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The concept of Food Loss and Waste (FLW) is a global challenge, and it is receiving increased attention from both the academic and policy sectors. This problem is becoming more widespread and is increasingly mentioned, especially in underdeveloped and developing countries. This article proposes to discuss the problem of FLW in the grape crops in order to offer solutions for reusing the leftovers from the crop. The paper will present the current state of knowledge of FLW, the supply and value chain of the crops and a detailed analysis of quantities produced, imported, exported and processed. This paper is based on the research done in the IPSUS project that considers the use of techniques for recovering recycled plant and seaweed proteins from raw materials. Also, the quantity, quality and upcycling opportunities of FLW along the value chain will be investigated. To analyse the quality and quantity of FLW from viticulture, an IoT system will be used to measure different environmental parameters such as air temperature and humidity, soil moisture and precipitation levels to estimate the quality and quantity of the harvest, an essential element in the concept of food loss and waste. The results of the research will demonstrate the importance of the reuse of grape crops thus offering new possibilities of development in the agricultural field in Romania.

articleTitle: Status Report of Training Development in the METIS Project Focusing on Test and Validation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The EU microelectronics sector needs to address serious talent gaps to increase its competitiveness. Considering this, the training/course development of MicroElectronics Training, Industry and Skills (METIS) project establishes an individual European collaboration developing a long-lasting framework to identify the major global biases affecting the region and provide strategic foresight, forecast increasing skill requirements, identify job rules/jobs of the future, create a sector skills strategy to assist the EU microelectronics industry in maintaining its leadership position globally, establish an EU Microelectronics Observatory & Skills Council to support European synergies toward the demands of data-driven technologies, such as AI, enabled by advanced microelectronics and associated skills requirements. This work presents the first task in the fourth work package (WP4.1) in the METIS project, which is about the development of the test and validation plan of the METIS curricula modules in real-life scenarios by the METIS partners under the guidance of Budapest University of Technology and Economics (BME). The delivery schedule and methods for the METIS curriculum and METIS modules, as well as the process for gathering user feedback, are all covered under the Test and Validation plan. The most important component of the WP4 is gathering user feedback and comments on the modules’ content, delivery methods, and organizational structure to improve METIS curriculum. The METIS curriculum and training will then be completed, and recommendations for mainstreaming and adopting the METIS curriculum will be developed.

articleTitle: Advanced Investigations of On-board Interconnection Structures using 2D/3D Electromagnetic Field Analysis Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents various advanced investigations of on-board interconnection structures using cutting-edge 2D/3D electromagnetic analysis techniques. The scientific work's main objective lies in the design and development of high-density interconnections within laminated substrates of complex integrated circuit packages. Specifically tailored for "flip-chip" technology chips/dies, the activity aims to scrutinize, optimize, and validate these structures according to stringent engineering requirements.

articleTitle: Performance of Lithium Ion Cells used in Electric Vehicles depending on their Internal Resistance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Internal resistance is a key parameter that defines the performance of a lithium-ion cell. The cell's power density, dissipation, efficiency and state of health (SoH) all depend on its internal resistance. Although ideally it should be a value as close as possible to zero, due to several factors it has a variable value from cell to cell. Internal resistance increases as a battery degrades. In this paper, the performance of 18650 lithium ion cells will be investigated according to internal resistance from three different manufacturers.

articleTitle: IoT System for Vine Disease Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In recent years, the concept of the Internet of Things has spread in most fields due to the multiple benefits it offers, so they have recently started to be used in viticulture, together with artificial intelligence. These two innovative technologies and classical methods can lead to a much more efficient and rapid prediction of diseases that may occur in grapevine culture. As a goal, the present work aims to detect diseases from the period when the evolution can still be prevented by minimizing the occurrence in which the cause can develop using an algorithm for predicting and comparing the data taken from IoT sensors with the data taken classically. The data preprocessing is presented in this paper for automatic disease identification.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of two types of filaments with COMSOL for electrothermal process
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This study consists of a comparative analysis and design of two filament types (coil and flat designs) in COMSOL from the point of view of temperature variations on the surface, correlated with the temperature thresholds used in the process of drying the sample solution prior to an analytical analysis. The filaments are intended to be used in a small-sized electrothermal vaporization device for simultaneous determination of volatile elements like Ag, Cd, Cu, Pb and Zn from liquid microsamples. A power supply controlled using LabView supplies the optimal current to the filament in order to provide the necessary power to the analyte drying and evaporation process. The temperature measurements for the drying stage showed that the control of the current injection time on the filament in the two-stage drying process can be a solution to optimize the process.

articleTitle: Control of the Energy Conversion in Radial Microactuators Using Conductive Polymers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Conductive polymers (CPs) represent new controllable and low cost materials for microactuation. During the electrochemical doping process, polymer changes its volume, when a voltage is applied. Different combinations have been studied and among them the combinations with the new CPs, like P(VDF-TrFE-CFE) Terploymer (PVTC) placed between polyaniline (PANI) electrodes, present higher conductivity, when there are used for radial microactuation. The cycle life of $10^{6}$ order justifies tuning the actuator performances. The operating structures were reproduced at molecular level with HFSS program (by Ansys). The tensile stress was of ca. $0.8-2.6 \mathrm{MPa}$, at operating voltages $\pm(1 \ldots 4) \mathrm{V}$. An energy conversion efficiency of about 30-50 % was obtained, but with peaks even higher, for a radial strain of up to 80%, depending on the actuator dimensions and doping level. Dopants like metals from nitrates or chlorides $\left(\mathrm{Au}^{+}, \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}\right.$ cations) or soaking acids $\left(\mathrm{HNO}_{3}\right)$ in PEDOT:PSS or BaZr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf> Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf> O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> in Terpolymer have been considered for increasing the electrical conductivity in the polymer matrix. The radial, respectively tangential strain of the $C P$ radial actuator has been determined and the simulation data have been used to calculate the energy conversion efficiency of the CP actuator. The method generates characteristic parameters of the optimal structure to be synthesized, for the highest energy conversion rate, considering also new dopants and CPs in combination.

articleTitle: IoT - Home Management Device for Temperature and Humidity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Smart Home Systems have gained significant popularity in the last decade as more and more users choose to invest in this industry and make their lives easier and more comfortable. This presentation will give an overview of the technology that is being used in Smart heating control systems. Development, design, and testing processes will also be described. The system described below has two main parts that are responsible for the configuration and control processes. Data is the most important aspect of systems like this and therefore this project uses a fast online database to store all user data. The database represents the bridge between the two parts of system, the hardware and software part, which is divide into another two parts, a real time application that runs at microcontroller level, and another one that interact directly with the user which running form a dedicate server.

articleTitle: Adaptive Battery Management System with Active Cell Balancing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The main goal of this paper is to present a method to implement and design an active Battery Management System (BMS) that could be connected to a lithium-ion battery pack composed of 18650 – type cells. On the other hand, in this paper we present how to design a flexible BMS module that could be easily adaptable to different battery configurations. Starting from a Photovoltaic panel used like a power supply for a DCDC converter, the paper present also the MPPT algorithm used in this application. The results obtained are presented like a comparison between a simulation method for the proposed system and the obtained experimental results.

articleTitle: Increasing Data Transmission Reliability using Pseudo-spread-spectrum Short-Range Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) have become a key technology in various fields, enabling efficient data collection and monitoring. However, the coexistence of Wi-Fi networks and WSNs operating in the 2.4GHz spectrum, such as those utilizing nRF24L01P modules, may be prone to interference and raise challenges to achieve a reliable data transmission. This paper aims to explore a novel approach to enhance data transmission reliability by employing pseudo-spread-spectrum short-range radio networks. The goal is to spread the spectrum of nRF24L01P modules over multiple channels, utilizing multiple radio receivers, each operating on a different channel, and enabling the transmitter to dynamically change its frequency if acknowledgements are not received. A comparative analysis has also been conducted to determine the effectiveness of spreading the spectrum in data transmission reliability enhancement.

articleTitle: High Efficiency Perovskite Solar Cells Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have attracted a lot of interest in the last decade, due to the remarkable improvement in efficiency. To analyse the performance of the cells, various software solutions could be used. In this paper, we simulated a solar cell consisting of an active layer with two perovskite absorbers (methylammonium lead iodide CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>PbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and methylammonium tin iodide CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>), using the software SCAPS 1-D. We investigated the effects of different thicknesses for each of the two layers, by keeping the total thickness of the active layers constant and we observed that CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> plays an important role in the efficiency of the solar cell, increasing the performance due to its lower band gap. Also, we compared the results to those obtained from a perovskite solar cell with a single active layer, having the same thickness as the cell with two absorbers, and we observed improved values of the efficiency for the structure with two active layers.

articleTitle: Thermal Energy Harvesting from Small Sources Using Thermoelectric Generators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper aims to design, use, and integrate a system based on thermoelectric generators (TEGs). TEGs can convert heat to electricity through the Seebeck effect and vice versa. They have low complexity. These devices denote a nonconventional method of electrical energy generation. The power supplied by TEGs is low, but still can be used in low power applications. The main obstacle to these elements usage is low efficiency, and, for high-power systems, dimensions are exceptionally large. By connecting at least five TEG elements in a series, they can supply a voltage of about 2 to 3V to a boost converter input and lighting some LED strings. The booster converter controller used in this application is the LT1930, with good characteristics. A single dc-dc converter is used to stabilise the voltage, because is cheaper than classic approaches, when a converter is used to maximise the harvested power and another one as a stabiliser. In our experimental setup, the heat source used to supply TEG elements is some candles and the cooling is done by a heat sink. The solution can be industrialised as a product useful in case of electricity shortage or in non-electrified areas.

articleTitle: Preemptive Real Time Operating System for Low Power Microcontrollers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In operating systems (OSs), there are two types of scheduling methods in which CPU resources are allocated: non-preemptive and preemptive scheduling. Embedded system developers generally create applications using a non-preemptive scheduler OS owing to limited resources and better control over the tasks and behavior of the system. With a non-preemptive scheduler, programming tasks and system functionalities are more complex as it does not permit interruptions other than the scheduler. By contrast, a preemptive scheduler allows for easier application development as each task is seen as an independent action or program that can be interrupted at any given time. Therefore, this paper, a scheduler algorithm implementation based on round-robin and priority algorithms for low -power microcontrollers. Combining these two algorithms increases the system performance because of improved resource allocation to the tasks executed.

articleTitle: Implementation of a High Accuracy Pupil Detection Algorithm Using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: A high-accuracy pupil detection algorithm implemented using neural networks is presented. The technique used is that of a classifier, the classes being defined according to the possible positions of the pupil center. In order to reduce the number of neurons and therefore the complexity of the network, a parallel architecture was used, the two coordinates of the pupil center being delivered by different networks. Training, testing and validation were done using eye images from three databases previously used in testing algorithms based on traditional image processing.

articleTitle: Embedded Scheduler with Task Reset Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Embedded systems play an essential role in our daily lives as they function behind the scenes to improve our experiences, streamline processes, and provide convenience. For example, in residential homes, embedded systems can provide security alarms through a network of sensors that detect intruders and detect fires and noxious gases. In smart houses, such systems have become indispensable as they automatically regulate the temperature based on the activity inside the house and external weather changes. These examples prove how embedded systems have been integrated perfectly in our everyday lives, offering comfort and optimizing processes. The primary component behind an embedded system is the microcontroller and the application written in its memory. The tasks of embedded systems are typically controlled via an operating system that manages its actions. However, at times, because of malfunctions or unexpected behavior, the system may freeze. To recover from such a situation, embedded systems may require end user intervention or a system reset using a watchdog interrupt handler. The paper presents an embedded scheduler with task reset capabilities. Through this approach, the system control and end user experience were considerably improved.

articleTitle: Data Switch in Long Line 1-Wire Networks for Monitoring System of Large Sensor Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: 1-Wire technology is used for communication between one master and many slaves, as low-cost small devices spatially distributed on large ranges. It provides two-way data transmission, signaling and power over a single line plus ground reference. Two parameters are important for 1-wire network performance: network radius and weight. The topology of 1-wire networks depends on the number of slave devices connected to the network and their spatial distribution along with the organization of interconnecting wires. If the number of slave devices is high, like in large arrays of sensors, the network topology is complex as a mixed of base topologies and this is a real challenge to make it reliable. Switched networks allow the increase in complexity without increasing as much of network weight and radius. The network is divided into segments, which are electronically switched one at a time. In this paper, a long line 1-wire network is considered for a low-cost monitoring system of large array of temperature sensors. To surpass the network limitations and to obtain a reliable network, a switched network with 3 segments is chosen. A new data switch is proposed using a low-cost embedded system. The switch is included into master microcontroller and the switching process is accomplished by software. The proposed switch works well and it implies a reliable functioning network.

articleTitle: Algorithms for Processing Signals of Driver Fatigue Detection Sensors in Traffic
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Fatigue, drowsiness while driving a vehicle are dangerous because many people are not aware of the consequences and dangers they are exposed to in road traffic.A system for detecting fatigue while driving a vehicle was created and a software was developed based on the coding of some algorithms for the analysis of the signals received from a VGA camera regarding the closing of the eyes of the vehicle driver. The system generates a signal compatible with the vehicle’s CAN network for the sudden reduction of travel speeds in order to avoid impact with obstacles or collisions between two vehicles in the event that a driver falls asleep at the wheel and heads towards another vehicle.The system is compatible with the specific conditions of the automotive field, an electronic module compatible from the point of view of the environment, the temperature range, the vibration spectrum and the operating conditions, into the memory of which the specialized real-time surveillance software will be loaded

articleTitle: A New Triple-Stacked Step-Up Converter for High-Voltage Gain
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents a novel three-stage stacked dc-dc boost converter. It can be used in applications where a high boost is required between the output and input voltage. The converter can be used to replace many conventional cascaded converters, but it will have only one active switch. The main dc values expressions for the converter are derived from the charge balance and volt-second balance equations. An analysis is then performed to study inductor currents, capacitive voltages, and the ripple effects. The design formulas and the semiconductor stresses are then provided based on them. A prototype is theoretically designed, and the operation of the converter is confirmed by simulation. Finally, a PCB prototype is proposed, the new topology is practically built, and experimental signals and measurements are acquired.

articleTitle: IR-Scanning vs. PSIM-Thermal Simulation concerning πT Stress Factor used in DC-DC Converter’s Reliability Calculation.
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Lately, many manufacturers from the power electronics branch have inserted information about the reliability of the product in the data sheet they offer by means of formulae, and diagrams but primarily through thermal images made in infrared (IR) technology in order to show the capsule temperature value for the device. This value of the temperature is compulsory and necessary for the engineer involved in the calculation of general reliability for the product in question. Then, a metric of reliability is established using that temperature by means of the thermal stress factor $\pi_{\mathrm {{T}}}$ and using a model provided by an international standard for reliability prediction. This paper provides a comparative view of results for the two methods exposed above highlighting the pros and cons of these two.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Temperature Sensor Made with Linqstat for Automotive Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper proposes the use of the Linqstat material as a temperature sensor, inserted into a support and then used to monitor the temperature in the engine compartment of a vehicle. First, some aspects related to temperature sensors with conductive film are reviewed. The steps leading to the creation of some types of temperature sensors with Linqstat are presented. A comparative analysis of two experimental models aimed at verifying the properties of the dedicated car sensor is made. The possibility of building dedicated temperature sensors for a certain temperature range with various applications is noted. Finally, the subsequent approach to the method and location of the sensor in the engine compartment and other areas where it is necessary to monitor the temperature in the indicated range is shown.

articleTitle: Intelligent green electricity management system
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In this study, a few solutions to optimize the electricity produced by photovoltaic systems proposed for residential buildings have been proposed, based on finding solutions for the management of the energy produced in photovoltaic systems. According to these results, an increase in the use of the energy produced for domestic consumption by approximately 30% can be proposed. For example, for a residential home with four persons, with an average monthly electricity consumption of 350 kWh, for hot water preparation, the average consumption reduces to 290 kWh.

articleTitle: Guidelines for Reducing Conductive Coupling Noise in Electronic Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents a comparison between two PCB layouts for a discrete Buck converter. One of the PCB layouts is designed using a combination of well-known and new techniques to reduce conducted noise, while the other is designed ignoring these techniques. Following laboratory measurements and Spice simulations with PCB parasitics, the noise levels of the two boards were attenuated to the desired values. The comparison between the two PCB layouts suggests the importance of implementing electromagnetic compatibility techniques and performing Spice simulations including PCB parasitics in switching power supply designs.

articleTitle: The Advantages of using IoT Technology in Monitoring and Dams Management
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This article discusses the advantages of using IoT technology in the monitoring and managing activity of hydro energetic buildings, like dams. The dams in any country represent a national interest good with a special importance for the country’s economy and for the safety of the population. Every single day, meticulous monitoring takes place in these buildings equipped with an extensive network of sensors and dataloggers. Communication between dataloggers is established using the RS485 standard protocol. The data is sent to a local server. Currently, there is a local database accessible exclusively to the staff of that unit. Our research is focused on increasing the visibility of data from dam buildings. Raspberry Pi is used like a bridge between physical quantities acquired by sensors and the virtual world. The system’s functions include monitoring, performing datalogging, and collecting real-time data on parameters that describe the behavior of constructions. Due to the characteristics of Raspberry Pi this can be more easily integrated into RS485 network. Taking advantage of the internet networking capabilities offered by this smart board, the data will be transmitted to a cloud database. This application can be accessed anytime and from anywhere through a web platform called ThingSpeak. This is a secure and safe web platform from anybody can visualize data in real time. A warning system can be added to this project in case the values are out of the standard range.

articleTitle: From Classic Grids to Smart Grids - Evaluating the Energy Consumption of the Public Lighting System in Cluj-Napoca
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents an inventory of the public lighting system components of Cluj-Napoca and identifies the types of electricity consumers, based on the total electricity consumption in the public lighting system in the city. An analysis of energy consumption over the period of one year is performed, to identify the consumption pattern. Existing optimal equipment and the one with potential for improvement are identified. Based on data from the field, the potential for reducing the energy used in the public lighting system by replacing sodium lighting devices with LED devices and with efficient telemanagement systems is estimated.

articleTitle: Database for E-Learning Platform of Digital Clothing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Skills of students and professionals in virtual prototyping of clothing require adaptation to the latest software technologies. Such software enables visualization of the fitted garments, customization of the garments according to personal requirements, faster time-to-market of the clothing products and integration of the entire production chain. Common software works as desktop application and requires a lot of technical and financial resources. This paper presents an e-learning platform destined for the training of students and professionals in clothing design. The e-learning platform is available as a web application and includes a digital design learning (DDL) page. The DDL page enables online fitting of fabric-based garments on human avatars and uses for this purpose a digital database. This database includes 49 digital fabrics, 33 digital garments, a set of human avatars as well as various fashion styles. The goal of preparing students and professionals in digital clothing design was assumed by a prestigious European partnership of six research and educational providers, under coordination of INCDTP – Bucharest. The Erasmus+ project DigitalFashion (www.digitalfashionproject.eu) is an ambitious, ongoing project (2022-2025).

articleTitle: PCB Design for Reduced Thermal Drift for Current Measurements Through Shunt Resistors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This study was conducted from the necessity to measure electrical currents through shunt resistors as precisely as possible by minimizing thermal drift. The methods used to minimalize the thermal effects, placement of sensing lines, current lines and via instalment were analysed on 6 shunt resistors placed on a PCB which was coated with black paint to normalize the emissivity of the board. The results were measured and compared using a thermal camera, at an ambient temperature of 25, at a nominal current of 20A and a voltage provided from a power supply of 5V. The results show that the most effective layout for shunt resistors for reduced thermal drift is the one with sense lines at the middle of the pads and with no misalignment with respect to the current path.

articleTitle: Improving accuracy of ultrasonic distance measurement with microcontroller and adaptive process formula.
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents an improved model for high precision measurements using ultra-sound mechanical waves, taking into account the thermodynamic characteristics of the propagation medium of mechanical waves. The characteristics of interest of the propagation medium are viscosity and density, that affect the propagation speed and the attenuation during the round trip from the emitter to the receiver due to reflexion. For this experiment we developed an electronic device containing sonic sensors and actuators, temperature and pressure sensors. The experiment considers two distinct cases of high accuracy of the speed of sound in fluids, namely for compressible fluids (air, nitrogen, etc.) and incompressible fluids such as water, alcohols and fuels. The experiment is also useful in the case of high precision determination of the depth of some water basins, the shape of river valleys and fuel levels in fuel tanks. The entire device is controlled by a microcontroller used to integrate the data from the sensors and to implement the calculation formula that represents the calculation model. The result of the entire process is displayed on an lcd screen and it is also sent using the serial data channel to ensure communication with other functional blocks.

articleTitle: From idea to prototype: Designing a CO2 detection sensor for industrial consumers using the Kano model and QFD’s House of Quality
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: CO2 detection sensors have a wide area of applicability in many industries, being extremely versatile and appreciated. When designing an innovative product, literature emphasizes that the voice of the customer is particularly important. Therefore, the purpose of the present study is to design a new detection sensor for industrial use by taking into consideration the requirements of its target audience. The methods used are the Kano model and the first matrix of the Quality Function Deployment (QFD) method, namely the House of Quality (HoQ). Nine representatives of different industry sectors from the Western part of Romania have completed a Kano and importance questionnaire, stating their viewpoint regarding 17 technical and design related characteristics of the sensor and sensor case. The results have been analyzed and transposed in the HoQ, where the design requirements have been hierarchized based on their importance. In the end, the prototype of the sensor case has been designed, providing the most relevant aspects expressed by the potential customers. The originality of the study resides in the fact that it applies specific quality tools in the design stage of a technical product intended for industrial use, validating their relevance in the final output.

articleTitle: Condition Monitoring on Inverters for Enhanced Reliability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The design of power converters must consider the maximum electrical ratings and the thermal limitations of the power semiconductor devices. Condition monitoring CM method [1] is one important way of increasing power semiconductor systems reliability selecting a physical measurement which indicates failures or degradation in a power system. CM (condition monitoring) requires knowledge of power semiconductors devices failure mechanism to establish failure indicators [2]. The operational temperature of the power semiconductor device gives reliability indications and can be used to monitor the condition of operational converters. The use of thermosensitive parameters (TSEP) to reveal the effects of temperature on the power device remains an attractive method of condition monitoring, suited for packaged devices. This paper seeks to generalize a new method to monitor condition of power semiconductors inside an operational inverter. This is accomplished combining temperature measurements with signals through a microcontroller from temperature sensors online and monitoring of temperature on the output power stage of an inverter with the help of an IR thermal camera. The method described does not interfere with the converter's diagram. Successful implementation of these techniques during the actual operation of a device has not yet been achieved [3].

articleTitle: Modelling, Simulation and Performance Analysis of K-Thermocouples using PSPICE
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Considering the lack of precise thermocouple models in the day-to-day circuit simulations, in the current work, the authors propose a Personal Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis (PSPICE) model for a K-type thermocouple made with Analog Behavioral Modelling (ABM) blocks. The paper presents the steps to be taken to obtain the model, so that the user can create, in addition to the model already created and presented in this paper, his own PSPICE model for other types of thermocouples, each with its own characteristic.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Usage of Solid State MOSFET Switches in Test Equipment for PSI5 Automotive Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The test equipment for automotive electronics industry is often used to assess the behavior of the ECUs (Electronic Control Units) in case of simulated faults. Since the sensors of electronic systems in a vehicle are placed in specific points of the car chassis, they must be interfaced with the electronic control units. For testing in a controlled environment (test laboratories) of these interfaces is needed to emulate the fault scenarios with the test equipment – short circuits, signal line interruptions, increased lines resistance, etc. A matrix of switches is able to cover most of the test scenarios. The more sensors and test scenarios, the more complex is the switch matrix. The development of solid-state switches based on field effect transistors in the last decades makes this switch type more attractive in this regard. Our research is focused on investigating the advantages and disadvantages of CMOS switches and MOSFET relays in automotive testing equipment, compared with electromechanical switches.Unlike electromechanical switches, the solid state MOSFET switches have no moving parts (no contact bouncing), and they are much smaller, which makes them attractive for compact systems and higher switching speed. At the same time, electrical parameters are more stable and predictable.

articleTitle: Handwritten letter recognition using mathematical morphology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In present days, a major step for letter recognition was made with the development of different applications which can convert from a captured image characters such as letters, numbers and so on. These captured images can contain letters generated by software installed on an electronic device (such as laptop, tablet) or letters generated by a human being on using a pen and a paper or using a digital pen and a tablet. In this paper our interest is to generate a deep neural network (DNN) for handwritten letter recognition and then to evaluate Romanian alphabet letters affected by noise. Due to fact that a DNN is not resistant to noise, mathematical morphology operators are used. The noise can appear in an image during acquisition.

articleTitle: Bi-positional Remote Object Reliable Control using Resistor Analogue Coding on Microcontroller Input
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In many safety automation processes, the position of a mechanical object with two stable states must be determined with a high degree of confidence and the information transmitted remotely. For one or more objects located at tens of meters from a control center, a microcontroller may be used to evaluate the voltage created through a resistive network that is set with the help of mechanical position sensors and actuated by the position of the controlled object. There are critical cases in which position interpretation errors, given by mechanical sensors, object-microcontroller connection cables, and microcontroller inputs failures are unacceptable, potentially leading to significant damage, or even physical harm to human beings (e.g., for railway barriers or other mechanical barriers, mechanical railway signals, or doors, access gates in premises). This research proposes a system that allows the microcontroller to precisely identify the state of the controlled object(s) by detecting cases of failure. Data transmission from the microcontroller to the point where the information is needed may be performed through any known communication technology and protocol (wired or wireless). The system is characterized by a particularly low cost, a minimum number of communication channels between the object and the microcontroller, and a wide range of environmental conditions to operate in.

articleTitle: Thermoelectrical Parameters of SiC PiN Diodes with New Die Attachment Ag Paste
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This study comes with electrical and thermal measurements for new formula of die attachment of silicon carbide SiC PiN diodes. A pressure less sintering process have been developed [1] using an Ag paste with a small addition of resin for the chip of the SiC PiN diodes. Obtaining the characteristics of this type of PiN diodes is the objective of this paper and interpretation of result can conduct to the improvement of the technology for the SiC PiN diodes. SiC based devices have several advantages over traditional silicon and gallium arsenide [2]. One advantage is high operating temperature of SiC devices, another feature of SiC is high saturation velocity of electrons [3], which enables SiC-based devices to operate at high frequencies. An important characteristic of diodes for power and pulse application is the switching time [2]. All these properties of SiC PiN diodes offer a large scale of application.

articleTitle: Speed Control Model of DC Motor Based on a Parameter Investigation Prototype
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents a MatLAB/Simulink speed control model for a DC motor. Besides the known datasheet parameters of the motor, an investigation prototype is used for determining the motor parameters needed for modelling. Based on these parameters, the systemic model of the motor was developed using equations describing the mechanical and electrical phenomena involved. The motor speed is controlled using two control loops (one for the armature current and the other, effectively, for motor speed) according to cascade control technique. The two controllers are tuned according to Kessler version of the modulus criterion (for current) and symmetrical criterion (for speed). The tuning of the PI controllers used for both loops was done both, by mathematical calculation based on model specific transfer functions, and by experimental method. The response of the system is also investigated both, in steady-state and transient regime.

articleTitle: Energy Management System for an Islanded Microgrid using Stochastic Dynamic Programming under Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Today, intelligent management techniques play an increasingly important role in achieving clean and profitable energy solutions. As energy consumption rises around the world, the complexity of effective strategies to manage our energy resources based on new technologies also grows. This research paper introduces a smart energy management scheme for an islanded microgrid containing photovoltaic panels, a geothermal generator, a biomass generator, and an energy storage system, considering the uncertainty of the PV power output. The microgrid’s proposed energy management method resolves the generator’s scheduling problem using stochastic-dynamic programming, focusing on day-ahead cost optimization. The development of this solution is done using the Matlab environment. The main objective is not only to minimize the daily cost of the microgrid but also to prolong the batteries’ life cycle. Three different cases are studied considering the functionality of the energy storage system.

articleTitle: A green mobile One Health laboratory for infectious disease epidemics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The MOBILISE initiative facilitates a streamlined and effective collaboration across sectors, disciplines, and borders in the management of disaster risks. It operates at both international and local levels, promoting the exchange of knowledge and coordination in the field of crisis management standardization. The implementation of an electric/hybrid truck platform, coupled with the utilization of solar and wind power, will effectively reduce CO2 emissions in accordance with the objectives outlined in the European Green Deal. The Technology Readiness Level 7 (TRL-7) will be employed to carry out field testing within the laboratory setting. Additionally, it aims to enhance the capabilities of first responders in all stages of emergency response, encompassing various types of disasters, whether caused by natural or human factors. The ultimate goal is to enable first responders to better prepare for their operational activities.

articleTitle: New Custom Boards for Teaching Digital Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Delivering high quality graduates is a constant concern in our University and Department. Motivating students is a permanent task and can prove difficult in some situations. A new line of practical experiments using dedicated boards was initiated in the Digital Integrated Circuits Laboratory with the goal of addressing the students’ interest in mind. These portable boards are meant to be borrowed to the students for their own experiments, can be tied together and are fully electrically protected. Microcontroller based excitation is also possible. The boards are fully configurable, all states are indicated with properly colored LEDs and protected against any wrong connection. Possible experiments range from functions implementation, including MSI circuits like decoders, multiplexers, adders to more elaborate trigger Schmitt applications. Most of experiments require only connection wires. The goal of this paper is to introduce the concept and the implementation of the first board of the new custom boards line.

articleTitle: Rapid Maintenance based improved design for omnidirectional controlled wheels for VirtuSphere system
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Designing for rapid maintenance requires an approach whereby the replacement of rapidly wearing sub-assemblies can be easily replaced while ensuring that the degree of wear can be tracked in real-time if possible. The redesign of the movement system of the Virtusfera platform by the authors previously led to an omnidirectional platform with increased integration facilities in virtual environments. The article presents two solutions for redesigning some subsystems that make up the new experimentally validated solution, presenting at the same time the study based on which the subsystems with the lowest reliability were identified and a proposal for a real-time tracking solution for those subsystems. Numerical simulations of the two solutions are presented, and conclusions and directions are formulated regarding the practical implementation of these subsystems based on the concept of design based on rapid maintenance.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Accuracy of Thermographic Inspections of Photovoltaic Modules
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Remote inspections of photovoltaic installations are an important factor for taking timely measures to increase their efficiency and reduce degradation. This study deals with the accuracy and uncertainty of thermal measurements of PV cells. An experiment is organized in order to compare the measured temperatures with means of contact sensor and contactless infrared cameras from different distance. The obtained results indicate significant difference in the measured peak temperatures with the different means. Furthermore, the temperature gradient of an affected cell depends strongly on the soiling area and could surpass $40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, which is a precondition for significant errors in the measured temperatures, i.e. it creates a significant uncertainty. Another important observation is that for the investigated polycrystalline module no hotspot was created if 6% or less of a cell’s area is covered.

articleTitle: Improving the Properties of Conducting Polymers in Self-Doping Variant
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Novel self-doped conducting polymers demonstrate improved physical properties, which can be controlled by modifying their structure. A simulation strategy for material properties analysis has been conceived, with help of the 3D HFSS program. Electroactivity of the polymer was the phenomenon of interest, considering that the counterions are covalently bound to the polymer backbone. A comparative analysis has been performed for the group: poly(p-methylpyridinium vinylene) (PMePyV); poly(sodium4-[(2,3dihydrothieno[3,4-b] [1, 4]dioxin-2-yl)methoxy]butane-2sulfonate) (S-PEDOT); poly(9,9-bis(4´-sulfonatobutyl) fluorene-alt-co-1,4-phenylene) (PFP); Poly(4-(Thiophen-3-yl Methyleneamino)benzene Sodium Sulfonate)) (PThSA). The conductivity is increased and the SDCP is stable, in comparison with anion/cations doped variants of similar monomers used for polymerization. In the frequency domain up to 10$^{6}$ Hz, the real part of the effective permittivity values are also higher, meaning more energy stored within the medium, which can be used for actuation. Permittivity imaginary part decreases in magnitude and its frequency peak is narrower, indicating lower dissipation in the material. An increasing of the actuation force of about 12-15 % is expected in these polymer species and losses decrease of ca. 5-7 %.

articleTitle: Development of Cost Effective and Environmentally Friendly Supercapacitors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the assembly and testing of supercapacitors, focusing on cost effective and environmentally friendly materials, assembly techniques, and performance evaluation. High-purity nickel foil and cellulose separators were selected as key materials. The assembly involved meticulous layering of materials, resulting in two supercapacitors named M1 and M2. Rigorous testing revealed promising results in terms of capacitance, equivalent series resistance (ESR), and self-discharge behavior. This research offers valuable insights into the development of efficient and reliable supercapacitors for diverse applications.

articleTitle: Monitoring Hospital Activity Through Petri Nets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has revolutionized several industries by optimizing and providing advanced services through the collection and analysis of data acquired via sensor networks. Furthermore, the introduction of the Web of Things (WoT) has resolved numerous challenges associated with IoT interoperability. IoT and WoT can benefit e-health systems through the collection and analysis of physiological data collected from patients using wearable devices or sensor networks. Moreover, radio frequency identification (RFID) technology is suitable for patient monitoring because it is a mature technology and passive RFID tags that store patient data are cost-effective. Therefore, the combination of the three technologies (i.e., IoT, WoT, and RFID) may afford a system in which patient data can be handled and monitored remotely and hospital staff can be optimally organized and managed. In this study, we propose a monitoring architecture based on RFID-enabled sensors that can analyze the availability and performance of hospitals in terms of health services using stochastic models.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Corrosion Assessment of Low-Ag SAC Lead-Free Solder Alloys
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The current work assesses the short-term and long-term electrochemical corrosion (ECC) behavior of SAC305 and SAC0307-Bi-xMn in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution. The short-term assessment was implemented by linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) which showed no significant difference in corrosion current density values among the investigated alloys. However, the long-term assessment represented by cyclic series of open circuit potential (OCP) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) illustrated that SAC0307-Bi-xMn exhibited superior long-term ECC performance, notably delaying the onset of localized corrosion initiation. It is believed that the combination effect of reducing Ag content in SAC alloys and doping with Bi and Mn enhance the corrosion resistance of the native oxide film on the SAC solder surface. Such findings illustrate the importance of the surface native (pre-existed) oxide film in postponing the commencement of local corrosion of SAC alloys in NaCl solution.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Usage of Solid State MOSFET Switches in Test Equipment for SENT Automotive Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The test equipment for automotive electronics industry is often used to assess the behavior of the ECUs (Electronic Control Units) in case of simulated faults. Since the sensors of electronic systems in a vehicle are placed in specific points of the car chassis, they must be interfaced with the electronic control units. For testing in a controlled environment (test laboratories) of these interfaces is needed to emulate the fault scenarios with the test equipment – short circuits, signal line interruptions, increased lines resistance, etc. A matrix of switches is able to cover most of the test scenarios. The more sensors and test scenarios, the more complex is the switch matrix. The development of solid-state switches based on field effect transistors in the last decades makes this switch type more attractive in this regard. Our research is focused on investigating the advantages and disadvantages of CMOS switches and MOSFET relays in automotive testing equipment, compared with electromechanical switches. Unlike electromechanical switches, the solid state MOSFET switches have no moving parts (no contact bouncing), and they are much smaller, which makes them attractive for compact systems and higher switching speed. At the same time, electrical parameters are more stable and predictable.

articleTitle: Textile and Plastic Materials Study for Radiofrequency Structure Fabrication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents an empirical examination and comparative analysis of dielectric properties pertinent to textile and plastic materials, which are prospective candidates for the construction of radio frequency (RF) structures. The investigation delineated involves the elucidation of dielectric parameters of these materials, followed by a juxtaposition with extant data. Following this, RF simulations were conducted to design and scrutinize various RF structures, including antennas and transmission lines, employing the analyzed materials. Physical models were fabricated based on these simulations, with their performance being assessed against the empirical findings. The methodological rigor of the investigation extended to measuring pivotal dielectric parameters such as the dielectric constant and loss tangent of an array of textile and plastic materials, utilizing validated measurement techniques.

articleTitle: Implementation of holonomic kinematics in industrial vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The forklift is an industrial vehicle used for transporting different loads indoors (warehouses) and outdoors. It usually has 2 prongs for lifting and 4 wheels. This prototype aims to solve the lack of maneuvering space typical in crowded warehouses by replacing the regular wheels with omnidirectional Mecanum wheels for different types of movement. It uses 2 dual motor drivers (H-Bridge) for the 12V DC motors and one driver for the lifting mechanism with high torque stepper motor. The power is supplied from a 11.1V 2700mAh LiPo for the motors and for the other circuits. The robot is controlled with a mobile phone.

articleTitle: Design of a Temperature Controller for an Oven
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper describes the design and implementation of an automatic temperature control system. The developed temperature controller is designed to control temperature in an oven. The temperature can be controlled manually or automatically with a temperature profile imposed by the user. A bi-positional controller is implemented for temperature control. In manual mode, the user will select the set-point and the upper and lower limits. The control system will maintain the temperature within the prescribed limits. In automatic mode, the user can select a temperature profile, and the control system will impose that the temperature follows the prescribed temperature profile.

articleTitle: TIE-M Plus: Promoting Structural Analysis Learning with Competition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper introduces the TIE-M Plus (Techniques of Interconnection in Electronics – Mechanical) student contest, extending the long-standing TIE environment. TIE-M Plus focuses on Finite Element Analysis (FEA) and includes two sections: Structural Analysis and Thermal Management Analysis. The paper proposes a competition workflow, discusses the construction and evaluation of the TIEM Structural Analysis subject, and addresses the challenges faced during its development. The TIE-M Plus contest provides students with a comprehensive electronics development experience incorporating structural and thermal aspects. The findings emphasize the importance of continuous student engagement to create meaningful educational opportunities that meet industry demands. Close communication with potential contestants during the early stages was essential to gauge their competencies and align them with private sector requirements. Overall, the TIE-M Plus contest aims to contribute to the advancements of STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) education and the practical application of electronics knowledge.

articleTitle: A Method to Control of a Semi-Autonomous Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper introduces a technological solution for emergency services, particularly firefighters. It’s a remotely controlled vehicle designed to traverse and explore hard-to-reach areas during fire incidents, significantly reducing the risk faced by the firefighters. By using state-of-the-art technologies such as PID controllers and sophisticated programming languages such as Python and C+ +, the system provides a user-friendly interface where operators can predefine the vehicles route on a 1:1 scale map. This innovative approach surpasses the limitations of traditional remote-controlled vehicles and offers a safer and more efficient method of assessing potential hazards.

articleTitle: Latency Hiding of Log-Depth Scan and Reduce Networks in Heterogenous Embedded Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper discusses methods, algorithmic examples and general principles regarding latency reduction methods for single chip Map-Reduce and Map-Scan many-core architectures. Processors designed for embedded systems suffer performance limitations (both performance and power consumption) when running intense instead of complex computations. A common solution is to add accelerators to the host processor in order to offload parts of the intense computations. We consider a Map-Scan-Reduce many-core architecture to be highly effective as a general-purpose accelerator and in this paper, we discuss the latencies introduced by the Scan and Reduce networks and ways in which to hide them based on practical applications and the solutions we have employed. Proper usage of pipelining technique and algorithmic improvements helps us obtain in simulations supralinear accelerations in relation to the number of processing cores used for the algorithms presented: matrixvector/matrix multiplication, FFT, pooling.

articleTitle: Improved Flying Probe-Inspired In-Circuit Tester for Practical Laboratory Activities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative, improved, and sensorless Flying Probe-Inspired In-Circuit Tester (FPICT) for verifying the interconnects of Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs). The proposed tester, due to its portability, can be easily deployed in laboratory environments for practical purposes. Thus, our research aims to demonstrate the effectiveness of the FPICT in increasing the learning rate of young scholars in Test Engineering Education (TEE). A total number of 16 high school students from "Caius Iacob" Technological High School of Electronics and Automation of Arad, Romania, were selected as the target group for the test platform studies. Before the practical laboratory activities, we performed a series of tests to evaluate the reliability of the improved FPICT.
