The experimental results show that the proposed FPICT is suitable for smaller and medium-sized PCBs and proves efficient regarding the probe’s positioning accuracy (99.06% for measurement testing), navigation time (an average of 8.20 seconds for single point testing), power consumption (an overall of 14.67W for all considered test cases), and cost (around 30 dollars). The obtained results indicate that the FPICT prototype passed the initial tests and can now be utilized in a learning environment for the final product validation stage.

articleTitle: Reliability enhancements for high-availability systems using distributed event streaming platforms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The effectiveness of a performant high-availability system can be measured by the transaction operations’ execution speed and reliability metrics. The performance and reliability of traditional database interactions can be improved through multiple techniques, including incorporating emerging technologies, such as distributed event streaming platforms, in the new or existent software infrastructure. This study is underlining the improvements that were obtained through Kafka integration with existing database operations by running a series of performance tests on two separate endpoints, that communicated with an independent software module. One endpoint used an asynchronous communication system, through event streams, and the other one used a traditional synchronous communication, through REST calls. Performance indicators such as throughput, error rate and execution time were extracted and analyzed, and it resulted that the data sent through Kafka had a 0% loss rate. Also, due to the numerous configuration options available, the reached throughput, using the asynchronous communication system, was more than 10 times higher. The study continued with an analysis of other event streaming platform vendors, with their particular features, disadvantages and other companies that use that specific technology. The final section is dedicated to a guide of best practices that ease the transition to an asynchronous messaging system between independent software modules, or just the addition of a new event streaming pipeline, and how to achieve performant and resilient communication, with configurable back-up mechanisms.

articleTitle: Chiplets and Next-gen Packaging Technologies in University Education
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Gordon Moore famously predicted in his ”Moore’s Law” paper that it might become more cost-effective to construct extensive systems using smaller, individually packaged functions interconnected together. More than half a century later, the structure of the System-on-a-Chip (SoC) changes significantly with the partitioning of a monolithic die into smaller chiplets: packaging becomes one of the main focuses when designing a chip and the way the initial functionality is partitioned between multiple chiplets and how these are interconnected means we have to shift our perspective to Systems in Package (SiP). Standards for interconnecting chiplets play a huge part in making chiplet technology the next evolutionary step in electronics. For this to be widely adopted across the industry there needs to exist specifications about electrical signaling, types of packaging, channels length, spacing, and routing between chiplets so that the chips of the future can have diverse functionality and use IP from different companies. Such standards have already emerged in the past two years and we will cover some of the proposed ideas. In the present paper, we propose solutions at the university curricula level to introduce the subjects mentioned above, as well as open-source tools which will enable students to practice theoretical notions about chiplets by designing and simulating virtual SiPs.

articleTitle: Energy efficient monitoring solution for lighting systems of hazardous areas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: To ensure proper lighting for improved safety and security in hazardous areas (e.g., road intersections, pedestrian crossings, bridges, or walkways), it is necessary to obtain real-time information regarding the state of lighting lamps, especially when their operating state changes. Modern lighting lamps are already equipped with suitable communication technologies, but there are many situations where simple ones are used, and investments in a complete system are prohibitive. In this research, the authors propose a flexible and cost-effective hardware solution which employs a microcontroller-based module to monitor the state of a lamp and send messages every time its state changes. The module is suitable for different types of communication technologies and may be installed with minimal or even zero intervention on the lamp power line. Two types of sensors are analyzed, as well as the possibility of powering the module from its own energy source, aiming to obtain the lowest possible energy consumption, and offering longer battery lifetimes than in the case of using the sleep mode of the microcontroller and of the communication module.

articleTitle: Innovative HDL Lessons Targeting the terasIC DE10-Lite Intel FPGA Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This work introduces students to hardware description languages and the integration of custom components in terasIC DE10-Lite FPGA boards using Quartus, Platform Designer, and Eclipse. Students learn to set up component connections and settings and make them work using Verilog HDL. Additionally, there’s a session focusing on creating a custom $\mathrm{I}^{2}\mathrm{C}$ component to communicate with an accelerometer using the $\mathrm{I}^{2}\mathrm{C}$ protocol. These hands-on sessions help students gain practical skills in designing and adding custom components to Intel Nios FPGA systems. These skills create a strong foundation for modernizing coursework in hardware description languages by teaching practical Verilog description for components and their integration into systems. In summary, this work helps students bridge the gap between theory and real-world implementations. As the digital world evolves quickly, these skilled engineers are well-prepared to lead innovation, influence industries, and contribute to the future of technology.

articleTitle: How to improve the scrap rate in data control modules using the DMAIC model and statistical analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Six Sigma represents a methodology designed for error-free processes throughout a company. It provides great statistical tools and the DMAIC systematic model which help reduce process variation in many different manufacturing companies, especially in the automotive domain. The present study aims to improve the failure rate in body control modules dealing with electrical overstress (EOS) caused by electrostatic discharge (ESD) events, in an automotive company situated in the Western part of Romania. Thirty hypotheses were taken in consideration and analyzed using statistical tools like correlation, regression, and trend analysis together with quality tools like Ishikawa diagram or Pareto analysis in a DMAIC approach. The corrective actions which were brought to the process were monitored to assure an acceptable process capability. The improvement actions decreased considerably the overall scrap rate. The results show that for the specific analyzed error message, the scrap costs have been reduced by 98.71%.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Diagnosis of Rotor Broken Bars Using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: An artificial intelligence system was implemented to accurately classify rotor faults in a three-phase induction motor. Fault detection and diagnostics, as part of the predictive maintenance program, is a data driven approach which contributes to the reduction of costs in the manufacturing industry. The system incorporates multiple procedures which restructure the data and decrease the necessary loading time into the memory. Preprocessing the information allows the selection of relevant features, scaling, and noise filtering. When designing the model, multiple architectures were analyzed with respect to the test accuracy until the optimum architecture was obtained. By filtering the transient state of the induction motor an additional increase of accuracy was noted. To increase the field reliability of the model, dropout and regularizers were added to the optimum architecture leading to a slight increase in accuracy. The obtained models were validated by using test data and with respect to the scientific literature.

articleTitle: A survey on the efficiency of the use of RFID technology in traffic management systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: With its many advantages and advances, UHF RFID (Ultra-High Frequency Radio Frequency Identification) technology has become a potent instrument in traffic control systems. This technology makes use of radio waves to wirelessly identify and track vehicles that have RFID tags, making it possible to monitor, manage, and optimize traffic in an effective manner. The use of UHF RFID technology in traffic management systems is essential for many applications.Monitoring and controlling traffic flow is a prominent application of UHF RFID technology in traffic management. Real-time traffic data, such as vehicle speed, volume, and occupancy, can be gathered by strategically placing RFID readers and antennae across road networks. This information is used to analyses traffic patterns, spot crowded regions, and make wise decisions to improve traffic flow. Based on the gathered data, traffic signal timing can be changed dynamically to ease congestion and increase efficiency.The paper investigates the effect of UHF RFID technology used as an auxiliary monitoring and control system of a road section. The considered road section is the access point that connects the western region with the Bucharest city Centre via the A1 highway. The road section presents a series of characteristics specific to congested traffic in an interurban scenario. Real traffic data were taken to demonstrate the high level of lane occupancy on the road segment, which serves as a critical access point in Bucharest. The novelty of this concept consists in the real-time monitoring and control of vehicles by means of a reception algorithm based on fuzzy logic-based approach to detecting a passive RFID Tag mounted on the considered cars using UHF RFID antennas.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Architecture for an Automated PV System with Self-Testing Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 29th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The current research presents a digital twin design for a self-testing automated Photovoltaic (PV) panel. The proposed digital twin, designed via Verilog language, is comprised of three main functions that emulate the PV system's data acquisition and solar tracking operations. The automated PV system, on the other hand, is a dual-axis stepper motor model controlled by the main Arduino Mega 2560 Microcontroller Unit (MCU) in conjunction with several sensor modules that monitor temperature, sunlight radiation, Ultra Violet (UV) level, and wind speed in real-time. This study focuses on constructing a hardware design for the axis calibration, wind gust protection, and solar tracking features. Additionally, we advance a novel Reconfigurable Built-In Logic Block Observer (ReBILBO) to evaluate the functionality of the wind speed module which moves the solar panel into the flat position. The experimental results show that the ReBILBO increases the fault coverage by almost 30% for adding 3 XOR gates, respectively 3 buffers to the standard BILBO architecture.
